articles.summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on Wednesday approved a groundbreaking new treatment for advanced pancreatic cancer that nearly doubled median survival in a clinical trial, marking what experts are calling one of the biggest advances against the deadly disease in decades. The drug, daraxonrasib, which will be sold under the brand name Rasonque, is approved for metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, the most common form of pancreatic cancer. Developed by Revolution Medicines, Rasonque is a once-daily pill designed to block RAS proteins that play a key role in driving tumor growth. The FDA approved Rasonque for adults with metastatic pancreatic cancer who have already received at least one cancer treatment, such as chemotherapy, or who cannot undergo combination treatment. The approval came approximately 6.5 months ahead of the FDA’s goal date, following an expedited review. “Today’s approval provides a critical new option for patients facing an extraordinarily difficult and historically hard-to-treat cancer. stories.summary: Not every woman is destined to become a biological mother. That doesn’t mean she can’t embody the essence of one through sacrifice, nurturing, humor, wisdom, and grace.
